Recreation Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the Community Services Department via email at
kshigenaga@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300­0791 at least 48 hours prior to
the meeting.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)

each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Recreation
Commission on any item of interest that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
Recreation Commission. Pursuant to state law, the Recreation Commission may not discuss or
take action on issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The
Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to
follow up on such items.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  MONDAY, JANUARY 9, 2023 AT 6:00 P.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Barth
Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson Solan,
  and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: Commissioner Tsai

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Commissioner Tam shared that he was informed by a resident that there is a large dog walking
group with off leash dogs at Lacy Park on Fridays. He inquired what measures are taken to ensure
the safety of patrons and that dogs are kept on leash at the Park. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
responded that if Park staff are present, they will advise the patrons of the rules; sometimes Code
Enforcement or the Police Department are called to help address the situation.

Chairperson Yen shared that he invited some neighbors to breakfast in hopes of getting to know
everyone better, and encouraged other Commissioners to do the same. He also shared his theme
for the Commission for the year which is to encourage the expansion of existing curriculum to
incorporate small or more intimate events.

NEW BUSINESS

1. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Tam moved, seconded by Commissioner Wu, to approve the minutes from
November 14, 2022.
 RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson
  Yen
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Tsai

2. DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson presented the staff report. Director Johnson shared that Commissioner Tsai
emailed staff prior to the meeting and suggested a snow play area and a better way to manage lines
at the next Tree Lighting Ceremony. Commissioner Wu shared that he attended the event and
heard from many residents that they enjoyed the sense of community. Chairperson Yen and Vice
Chairperson Solan inquired how program ideas, new and old, can be incorporated into the work
plan. Director Johnson responded that suggestions are accepted throughout the year since there
has not been an opportunity to strategically plan with the Commission, and suggestions can be
shared as part of their Commissioner Reports.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

3. RECREATION DIVISION SCHEDULE OF FEES FOR SERVICE FOR FISCAL YEAR
  (FY) 2023-24

Director Johnson presented the staff report and read Commissioner Tsai’s feedback she received
via email prior to the meeting. Commissioner Tam expressed that fees for Open Swim and Lap
Swim should stay the same since the pool is significantly smaller than others. Director Johnson
explained that the City does not own the pool, and has to pay a high rental fee, unlike most other
cities in the area who own their pools. Chairperson Yen inquired how recommendations for Senior
Trips can be communicated. Director Johnson responded that ideas can be shared with staff, and
she hopes for a planning session with the Commission in the future where all can provide ideas and
recommendations. There was discussion by the Commission regarding the location and participation
numbers of the Family – All Ages programs; what the increased 4th of July admission costs would
cover and their thoughts on the proposed pricing; details of the Lacy Park After Dark Camp Out;
the various permits available at Lacy Park; and how pricing was established for San Marino
Community Center rentals.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Wu moved, seconded by Commissioner Tam, to support staff’s recommendations
to the FY 2023-24 Schedule of Fees for Service.
